fundamentals.name: Cerebras Systems Inc.
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Cerebras Systems Inc. operates as an artificial intelligence infrastructure company. It designs and manufactures an AI compute platform that comprises of proprietary systems and software that is delivered in racks for deployment in data centers up to supercomputer scale. The company's pioneering wafer-scale engine, a chip encompassing a silicon wafer, designed to enable higher performance and speeds than GPUs for the computational demands of inference, Generative AI, and other AI applications. Its customers include hyperscalers, foundation model labs, AI-native and digital-native businesses, enterprises, and leaders of Sovereign AI initiatives. The company has operations in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and internationally. Cerebras Systems Inc. was founded in 2015 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

judgment.summary: Extremely high valuation with significant operating losses and negative free cash flow, despite impressive revenue growth.
positives: Revenue growth 1474.4% YoY — exceptionally high top-line expansion.
Return on equity 38.4% — strong on paper, but likely distorted by negative book value or other factors given losses.
Current ratio 2.15 and Quick ratio 1.64 — healthy short-term liquidity.
Total debt $27.97M vs $209.50M cash — manageable leverage.
negatives: Trailing P/E 488.26 and Price/Sales 90.41 — valuation is extremely stretched.
Operating margin -30.7% and Free cash flow (TTM) $-622.92M — the company is not profitable and burns significant cash.
Profit margin 46.6% — this appears to be an anomaly given the negative operating and FCF, possibly due to one-time gains or accounting treatments.
Return on assets -5.3% — negative return on its asset base.

news.paragraph: Cerebras Systems (CBRS) is facing headwinds after its CEO reportedly stated the company works with all AI component makers except Nvidia. This news has caused the stock to dip in pre-market trading and has been highlighted by several financial news outlets, including GuruFocus and Yahoo Finance. The company's valuation and post-IPO volatility have also been subjects of recent discussion.
